bull_bear.body:
- In-house manufacturing facility with stringent quality control mechanism - ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001: 2015, ISO 14001: 2018 and ISO 3834-2:2021 certified, with an extensive testing suite (hardness tester, ultrasonic flaw detector, MPI, spectrometer, adhesion tester, DGT gauges) enabling streamlined inventory management, minimised production time and cost effectiveness
- Order Book - orders in hand from 6 customers aggregating Rs. 35,981.72 lakhs as of March 31, 2026, providing visibility on future revenues
- Well-positioned to capture growth opportunities - rising demand for windmill towers driven by the global push for renewable energy adoption, with a limited number of qualified suppliers in the market enhancing competitive advantage
- Strategically located manufacturing facilities in Koppal (Karnataka) and Kutch (Gujarat), across ~48.05 acres along major highways, close to wind energy development zones in the two states that account for 180.8 GW and 169.3 GW of wind potential and ~40% of India's installed wind capacity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Limited operating history in the current line of business and Promoters without prior significant experience in the wind energy infrastructure segment — Incorporated January 2021, commenced operations in the windmill tower segment only in 2023; Promoters' two decades of experience is in other industries, so understanding of industry dynamics, customer requirements and supply-chain complexity rests on a short track record and may not be sufficient for investors to assess future performance.
- Single-segment revenue concentration in Tower Manufacturing and Fabrication — The segment accounted for 94.36%, 99.95% and 81.23% of total revenue from operations for FY ending March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024; exposure to demand reduction, competition from regional and national players, superior/cheaper technology, raw-material price and availability swings, and regulatory or import-duty change.
- Seasonal and cyclical variation in the business — Installation of wind turbine towers at project sites is significantly impacted during the monsoon/rainy season due to unfavourable weather and logistical constraints, causing fluctuations in results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- Customer concentration in the order book — The entire order book of Rs. 35,981.72 lakhs as of March 31, 2026 comes from just 6 customers (Customer A to Customer F), so loss of or delay from any one customer would materially affect the revenue visibility the Company relies on.
- Geographic concentration of revenue in Karnataka — Karnataka contributed 93.87% of revenue from operations in FY 2025-26 (99.95% in FY 2024-25), leaving results exposed to wind project activity and conditions in a single state despite facilities in two states.
- Under-utilised installed capacity — Capacity utilization was 38.00%, 45.00% and 48.17% in FY 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 against an annual capacity of 612 towers; the newly commissioned Kutch facility adds capacity that must still be filled, and fixed-cost absorption depends on raising volumes.
- Dependence on client-supplied materials and an ex-works conversion model — Clients supply plates, flanges, internal assemblies, door frames and paint and are responsible for transporting finished towers, so production schedules and throughput depend on the timeliness and quality of client-supplied inputs rather than the Company's own procurement.
- Borrowing levels requiring Rs. 11,500.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds for repayment/pre-payment — The principal object of the Fresh Issue is repayment and/or pre-payment, in full or part, of borrowings of Rs. 11,500.00 lakhs, indicating a leveraged balance sheet ahead of listing; RoCE (23.05% in FY26) sits well below RoNW (40.92%).

business.body: The Company manufactures windmill towers, focusing on fabrication of towers from heavy and precision steel components customized to client requirements in the wind energy sector. Towers are tubular steel structures rolled from heavy steel plates, longitudinally and circumferentially welded and made in multiple cylindrical sections (commonly five, typically 140 metres in height) for road transport and on-site erection using flanges and bolts. Products are supplied to marquee customers that are Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) of Wind Turbine Generators (WTG) and companies in the renewable energy sector; 100% of revenue is B2B.

outlook.body: The Company operates Unit I at Koppal, Karnataka across approximately 20.75 acres with an installed annual production capacity of 420 windmill towers (up to 35 towers per month). To meet growing demand in the wind energy sector it commenced operations at a new manufacturing facility at Lakadia, Bhachau, Kutch, Gujarat in March 2026, adding production capacity of 16 windmill towers per month. The two facilities together span 48.05 acres with an annual capacity of 612 towers, and the Company states it will continue to invest in capacity enhancement and operational expansion to further increase production capacity. The Karnataka and Gujarat locations were chosen for proximity to wind energy development zones and major highways, enabling direct transportation of finished products to assembly sites, port facilities or end customers and reducing transit time and logistics costs.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Cost of goods sold (cost of materials consumed, purchase of stock in trade and changes in inventories of finished goods) was Rs. 4,528.29 lakhs, Rs. 2,365.07 lakhs and Rs. 1,116.48 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, representing 30.09%, 20.65% and 38.81% of revenue from operations - a swinging material-cost ratio is a key margin lever
- Client-supplied material model: the client supplies essential raw materials such as plates, flanges, internal weldable parts, internal assemblies, door frames and paint, which the Company logs, verifies and fabricates - reducing the Company's own raw-material outlay
- Capacity utilization improving from 38.00% (FY 2023-24) to 45.00% (FY 2024-25) to 48.17% (FY 2025-26) alongside production of 114, 135 and 210 windmill towers - operating leverage/fixed-cost absorption
- Product mix concentrated in Tower Manufacturing and fabrication (Rs. 13,518.76 lakhs of Rs. 14,326.69 lakhs in FY 2025-26) with residual Boiler Accessories & Paper machinery parts and scrap sales
- Ex-works delivery model - finished goods are made available for client pickup from factory premises and transportation of finished towers to project sites is the responsibility of clients, limiting logistics cost exposure
- Geographic revenue mix shifting, with Karnataka at 93.87% of FY 2025-26 revenue and Gujarat rising to 6.13% following commencement of the Kutch facility
- Raw materials (primarily Mild Steel plates, plus shots and grits, paint, welding rods, plasma power sources, oxy-fuel stations, grinding wheels) are primarily sourced from local suppliers in India
- Seasonality: installation of wind turbine towers at project sites is significantly impacted during the monsoon/rainy season, causing fluctuations in results of operations and cash flows

business_ops.seasonality: "Our Company's business is inherently seasonal in nature, with the installation of wind turbine towers at project sites being significantly impacted during the monsoon/rainy season due to unfavourable weather conditions and related logistical constraints. Such conditions often cause delays in project execution during the April-September period, which in turn impacts the demand for our towers and results in comparatively lower sales during this period. Consequently, our revenues and profitability tend to be lower in the monsoon season and higher during periods of favourable weather conditions." Half yearly sales turnover (Rs. in lakhs): April-September 4,137.16 (28.88%) in 2025-26, 1,553.72 (19.77%) in 2024-25, 1,595.19 (29.50%) in 2023-24; October-March 10,189.54 (71.12%) in 2025-26, 6,305.14 (80.23%) in 2024-25, 3,811.45 (70.50%) in 2023-24. Combined with cyclical variations in the renewable energy industry, this may lead to considerable fluctuations in financial performance across quarters or half-yearly periods.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Client-supplied material / conversion (job-work style) model on the tower line: the business process is Order Confirmation, then "Client Supplies Materials" - "The client supplies essential raw materials such as plates, flanges, internal weldable parts, internal assemblies, door frames, and paint" - followed by material matching and verification, production, final checklist and inspection in the presence of a client representative, issue of a Work Completion Certificate, invoicing and Delivery (Ex-Works) where the client or their designated logistics partner arranges pickup from the company premises. Manufacturing is in-house and fully integrated on-site across 22 stages (CNC cutting, beveling, rolling, longitudinal seam welding, re-rolling, ultrasonic testing, flange fitting, can-to-can fitting, weld inspection inside/outside, full-section UT, bush fit-up and welding, door fit-up and welding, ring flange bracket, surface blasting, primer coating, final paint/PU coating, orange marking, client logo application and final assembly), with all plant and machinery fully owned by the company and an in-house laboratory and testing equipment. "The in-house manufacturing operations enable us to stream line inventory management and production process resulting into maintenance of high-quality production standards, minimizing production time and bringing cost effectiveness." Raw materials are primarily Mild Steel (M.S.) plates plus shots and grits, paint, welding rods, electric plasma power sources for cutting, oxy-fuel stations, grinding wheels, ladders, lightning protection systems and platforms; "All raw materials are procured domestically from local suppliers" - geographical classification of raw material procured shows Imported Goods of Rs. 20.98 lakhs (0.25%) in FY 31-03-2026 versus Indigenous Goods Rs. 8,371.08 lakhs (99.75%), and nil imports in FY 31-03-2025 and FY 31-03-2024. Cost of raw material consumed was Rs 4,731.58 lakhs, Rs 2,500.72 lakhs and Rs. 1,915.92 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. overview.business_model: The Company fabricates windmill towers as tubular steel structures made of multiple cylindrical sections (commonly five per tower), rolled from heavy Mild Steel (M.S.) plates, longitudinally and circumferentially welded and joined through flanges and bolts during erection at the project site; sections are transported by road to the project site. It sells to Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) of Wind Turbine Generators ("WTG") and companies in the renewable energy sector. Revenue is reported as Tower Manufacturing and fabrication (Rs. 13,518.76 lakhs in FY 31-03-2026), Boiler Accessories & Paper machinery parts (Rs. 18.00 lakhs) and Others, being sale of weldmash / scrap (Rs. 789.93 lakhs). Raw materials (M.S. plates, shots and grits, paint, welding rods, ladders, lightning protection systems, platforms, etc.) are primarily sourced from local suppliers in India; cost of goods sold was Rs. 4,528.29 lakhs, Rs. 2,365.07 lakhs and Rs. 1,116.48 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024, representing 30.09%, 20.65% and 38.81% of revenue from operations.

genesis.founding_story: Ayush Nimish Vashi and Bhavin Navinchandra Desai were the initial subscribers to the Memorandum of Association, subscribing 50,000 Equity Shares each. The Company commenced operations pursuant to a declaration for commencement of business dated April 19, 2021 filed with the Registrar of Companies, Ahmedabad, and commenced commercial operations in April 2021 initially focusing on fabrication of weldmesh and assembly of boiler accessories and paper machinery parts. Building on that foundation and leveraging its expertise in steel fabrication, it strategically shifted into the wind energy sector in 2023 and has since focused on manufacturing fabrication components for wind turbine towers. The Company is led by Promoters and Executive Directors Nimish Kumar Rameshchandra Vashi (Chairman & Managing Director, associated with the Company since February, 2025) and Ayush Nimish Vashi (Whole-Time Director, associated since incorporation).

concerns_observed: No valuation anchor exists: the DRHP states twice that 'There are no listed companies in India that are engaged in a business similar to that of our company', so neither accounting-ratio nor KPI peer comparison is provided, P/E is shown as [.], and the Company's own risk factor on this is graded high severity. The 8 peers in peers_internal are our own keyword matches on products, not DRHP-stated comparables, and are not a pricing benchmark.

The offer buys no growth: the only quantified object is Rs 11,500.00 lakhs of borrowing repayment plus an unquantified general corporate purpose - project.total_cost_lakhs is null, there is no capex object, no machinery or quotation annexure, and no funding mix. The Rs 13,00,800-share Offer for Sale by Nimish Kumar Rameshchandra Vashi brings no proceeds to the Company at all.

Leverage was built hard and fast right before the offer: total outstanding indebtedness Rs 12,824.76 lakhs at March 31, 2026 (secured portion Rs 12,308 lakhs) against net worth of Rs 8,951.16 lakhs; FY26 financing inflow of Rs 8,030.36 lakhs included Rs 9,029.27 lakhs of fresh long-term borrowing against only Rs 2,030.05 lakhs repaid, and all fund-based facilities sit with a single lender, Bank of Baroda. Rs 516.76 lakhs of unsecured loans (4.03% of total indebtedness) are recallable at any time.

The newly commissioned capacity is barely running: Kutch Unit-II utilisation is 8.04% in FY26 (actual production 4,822.20 MT in its single operating month, March 2026) and Karnataka 41.74%; company-level tower utilisation is 48.17%. Under-utilisation is itself a high-severity risk factor in the DRHP.

Governance turnover is unexplained: both independent directors appointed April 1, 2025 - Balwant Pooranmal Tayal and Navin Kumar Kewalchand Bhurat - resigned with effect from June 19, 2025, with no reason recorded, and replacements were appointed w.e.f. June 20, 2025. No director has previously served on the board of a listed company, and committee memberships are not populated in the extract.

Related-party density is high: 75 related-party transaction lines. Promoter/MD Nimish Vashi took loans of Rs 1,442.24 lakhs in FY26 (repaid Rs 1,039.58 lakhs); group company Darpan Infrastructure Private Limited lent Rs 1,389.52 lakhs (FY24) and Rs 1,018.67 lakhs (FY25), charged Rs 97.60 lakhs as commission for a corporate guarantee in FY26, is the landlord of the registered office, and until November 30, 2023 held 51% of the Company before transferring control to the promoter. Darpan's own financials are not set out in the DRHP.

Concentration on every axis, with no long-term contracts on either side: top-1 customer 29.32% and top-5 78.75% of FY26 revenue; top-10 suppliers 90.11% of FY26 purchases (up from 72.44% in FY24); Karnataka 93.87% of FY26 revenue; Tower Manufacturing and Fabrication 94.36% of FY26 revenue. The DRHP states there are no long-term agreements with customers and none with suppliers.

Working capital absorbs the profit: inventory days 252.85 / 175.06 / 202.69 (FY26/FY25/FY24); inventories rose to Rs 5,068.78 lakhs from Rs 1,205.01 lakhs and trade receivables to Rs 3,894.54 lakhs from Rs 2,516.61 lakhs, so FY26 CFO of Rs 1,843.94 lakhs converts only about half of the Rs 3,662.83 lakhs PAT. Debtor days, creditor days and the cash conversion cycle are blank in the source and trade payables are null for all three years.

Corporate-records hygiene is weak and graded high severity by the extraction: clerical errors in PAS-3 filings, inaccuracies in the altered MOA, incorrect first-financial-year details and incorrect figures in passed resolutions; past board reports omitted disclosure of funds accepted from directors/relatives and the CSR report; BEN-2 filed late; DPT-3 filed with clerical mistakes that cannot be revised; 14 delayed ROC forms across FY2021-22 to FY2025-26 (delay-days column not populated in the source).

Property and title are unresolved at both sites: certain Kutch properties were acquired from a seller not in possession of the original registered title deeds, reported lost (FIR dated October 11, 2021, Anjar Police Station; sale agreement dated October 14, 2021); the registered office is rented from group company Darpan at Rs 5,000 per month; and 19 open storage plots at Koppal are on third-party rent with 'no activity being carried out on any of these plots'. Some occupancy documents are unregistered under the Registration Act, 1908.
Manufacturing unit 2 at Kutch carries no insurance policy, and there is no workmen insurance, product liability or keyman cover.

[Addendum dated 27-Jul-2026, filed 28-Jul-2026 - NOT covered by our DRHP extraction] A new risk factor absent from the 358-page DRHP: a vendor has used the Company's Koppal manufacturing facility address as its own place of business for GST registration, pursuant to an NOC issued by the Company, which may draw GST scrutiny or inspection to the facility.

Pre-offer capital engineering compresses the look-back: a 9:10 bonus of 86,85,000 shares on April 25, 2025 (within ~14 months of the DRHP date), followed by the two Rs 101 placements; promoter average cost of acquisition is Rs 7.65 and Rs 5.26 per share, below the Rs 10 face value, and the DRHP carries this as its own risk factor.

Revenue is strongly second-half weighted on monsoon-driven installation timing: April-September contributed 28.88% / 19.77% / 29.50% versus October-March 71.12% / 80.23% / 70.50% for FY26/FY25/FY24, so any single half-year is not representative.

The restated financial statements were furnished by a peer-reviewed chartered accountant (S.R. Goyal & Co.) who is not the statutory auditor (M/s G.B. Laddha & Co. LLP), disclosed as a risk factor in the DRHP itself.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures windmill towers, focusing on fabrication of towers from heavy and precision steel components customized to client requirements in the wind energy sector. Towers are tubular steel structures rolled from heavy steel plates, longitudinally and circumferentially welded and made in multiple cylindrical sections (commonly five, typically 140 metres in height) for road transport and on-site erection using flanges and bolts. Products are supplied to marquee customers that are Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) of Wind Turbine Generators (WTG) and companies in the renewable energy sector; 100% of revenue is B2B.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Client-supplied material / conversion (job-work style) model on the tower line: the business process is Order Confirmation, then "Client Supplies Materials" - "The client supplies essential raw materials such as plates, flanges, internal weldable parts, internal assemblies, door frames, and paint" - followed by material matching and verification, production, final checklist and inspection in the presence of a client representative, issue of a Work Completion Certificate, invoicing and Delivery (Ex-Works) where the client or their designated logistics partner arranges pickup from the company premises. Manufacturing is in-house and fully integrated on-site across 22 stages (CNC cutting, beveling, rolling, longitudinal seam welding, re-rolling, ultrasonic testing, flange fitting, can-to-can fitting, weld inspection inside/outside, full-section UT, bush fit-up and welding, door fit-up and welding, ring flange bracket, surface blasting, primer coating, final paint/PU coating, orange marking, client logo application and final assembly), with all plant and machinery fully owned by the company and an in-house laboratory and testing equipment. "The in-house manufacturing operations enable us to stream line inventory management and production process resulting into maintenance of high-quality production standards, minimizing production time and bringing cost effectiveness." Raw materials are primarily Mild Steel (M.S.) plates plus shots and grits, paint, welding rods, electric plasma power sources for cutting, oxy-fuel stations, grinding wheels, ladders, lightning protection systems and platforms; "All raw materials are procured domestically from local suppliers" - geographical classification of raw material procured shows Imported Goods of Rs. 20.98 lakhs (0.25%) in FY 31-03-2026 versus Indigenous Goods Rs. 8,371.08 lakhs (99.75%), and nil imports in FY 31-03-2025 and FY 31-03-2024. Cost of raw material consumed was Rs 4,731.58 lakhs, Rs 2,500.72 lakhs and Rs. 1,915.92 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. State-wise raw material procurement is concentrated in Gujarat (74.03% / 32.72% / 67.65%), Karnataka (15.46% / 31.16% / 9.71%) and Maharashtra (8.52% / 33.21% / 11.89%) for 31-03-2026 / 31-03-2025 / 31-03-2024. Logistics: "The transportation of steel plates and other raw materials to the manufacturing facility, as well as the delivery of finished goods to customers, is generally arranged by the respective suppliers and customers. Accordingly, the Company does not have any dedicated logistics arrangements for these activities." The Company engages a logistics service provider for sending semi-finished goods for job work and receiving them after processing, and for transporting finished goods from the manufacturing facility to the storage area, and owns one vehicle used for minor logistics and internal transportation. Collaboration: "Our Company has so far not entered into any technical and financial collaboration agreement with the third party." No long-term supply arrangements with suppliers and no long-term agreements with customers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Cost of goods sold (cost of materials consumed, purchase of stock in trade and changes in inventories of finished goods) was Rs. 4,528.29 lakhs, Rs. 2,365.07 lakhs and Rs. 1,116.48 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, representing 30.09%, 20.65% and 38.81% of revenue from operations - a swinging material-cost ratio is a key margin lever
- Client-supplied material model: the client supplies essential raw materials such as plates, flanges, internal weldable parts, internal assemblies, door frames and paint, which the Company logs, verifies and fabricates - reducing the Company's own raw-material outlay
- Capacity utilization improving from 38.00% (FY 2023-24) to 45.00% (FY 2024-25) to 48.17% (FY 2025-26) alongside production of 114, 135 and 210 windmill towers - operating leverage/fixed-cost absorption
- Product mix concentrated in Tower Manufacturing and fabrication (Rs. 13,518.76 lakhs of Rs. 14,326.69 lakhs in FY 2025-26) with residual Boiler Accessories & Paper machinery parts and scrap sales
- Ex-works delivery model - finished goods are made available for client pickup from factory premises and transportation of finished towers to project sites is the responsibility of clients, limiting logistics cost exposure
- Geographic revenue mix shifting, with Karnataka at 93.87% of FY 2025-26 revenue and Gujarat rising to 6.13% following commencement of the Kutch facility
- Raw materials (primarily Mild Steel plates, plus shots and grits, paint, welding rods, plasma power sources, oxy-fuel stations, grinding wheels) are primarily sourced from local suppliers in India
- Seasonality: installation of wind turbine towers at project sites is significantly impacted during the monsoon/rainy season, causing fluctuations in results of operations and cash flows

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expanding manufacturing and production capacities - continue to invest in capacity enhancement and operational expansion to cater to rising market demand in the wind energy sector
- Reducing operating cost and improving operational efficiencies - increase economies of scale, better absorb fixed costs, improve capacity utilization through higher production volumes, and manage supply chain costs through optimal inventory levels and economic orders
- Focus on consistently meeting customer specifications and quality standards - continuous review of products at different stages, timely corrective measures on deviations, to enhance customer trust and obtain repeat orders

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company operates Unit I at Koppal, Karnataka across approximately 20.75 acres with an installed annual production capacity of 420 windmill towers (up to 35 towers per month). To meet growing demand in the wind energy sector it commenced operations at a new manufacturing facility at Lakadia, Bhachau, Kutch, Gujarat in March 2026, adding production capacity of 16 windmill towers per month. The two facilities together span 48.05 acres with an annual capacity of 612 towers, and the Company states it will continue to invest in capacity enhancement and operational expansion to further increase production capacity. The Karnataka and Gujarat locations were chosen for proximity to wind energy development zones and major highways, enabling direct transportation of finished products to assembly sites, port facilities or end customers and reducing transit time and logistics costs.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house manufacturing facility with stringent quality control mechanism - ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001: 2015, ISO 14001: 2018 and ISO 3834-2:2021 certified, with an extensive testing suite (hardness tester, ultrasonic flaw detector, MPI, spectrometer, adhesion tester, DGT gauges) enabling streamlined inventory management, minimised production time and cost effectiveness
- Order Book - orders in hand from 6 customers aggregating Rs. 35,981.72 lakhs as of March 31, 2026, providing visibility on future revenues
- Well-positioned to capture growth opportunities - rising demand for windmill towers driven by the global push for renewable energy adoption, with a limited number of qualified suppliers in the market enhancing competitive advantage
- Strategically located manufacturing facilities in Koppal (Karnataka) and Kutch (Gujarat), across ~48.05 acres along major highways, close to wind energy development zones in the two states that account for 180.8 GW and 169.3 GW of wind potential and ~40% of India's installed wind capacity

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Limited operating history in the current line of business and Promoters without prior significant experience in the wind energy infrastructure segment — Incorporated January 2021, commenced operations in the windmill tower segment only in 2023; Promoters' two decades of experience is in other industries, so understanding of industry dynamics, customer requirements and supply-chain complexity rests on a short track record and may not be sufficient for investors to assess future performance.
- Single-segment revenue concentration in Tower Manufacturing and Fabrication — The segment accounted for 94.36%, 99.95% and 81.23% of total revenue from operations for FY ending March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024; exposure to demand reduction, competition from regional and national players, superior/cheaper technology, raw-material price and availability swings, and regulatory or import-duty change.
- Seasonal and cyclical variation in the business — Installation of wind turbine towers at project sites is significantly impacted during the monsoon/rainy season due to unfavourable weather and logistical constraints, causing fluctuations in results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- Customer concentration in the order book — The entire order book of Rs. 35,981.72 lakhs as of March 31, 2026 comes from just 6 customers (Customer A to Customer F), so loss of or delay from any one customer would materially affect the revenue visibility the Company relies on.
- Geographic concentration of revenue in Karnataka — Karnataka contributed 93.87% of revenue from operations in FY 2025-26 (99.95% in FY 2024-25), leaving results exposed to wind project activity and conditions in a single state despite facilities in two states.
- Under-utilised installed capacity — Capacity utilization was 38.00%, 45.00% and 48.17% in FY 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 against an annual capacity of 612 towers; the newly commissioned Kutch facility adds capacity that must still be filled, and fixed-cost absorption depends on raising volumes.
- Dependence on client-supplied materials and an ex-works conversion model — Clients supply plates, flanges, internal assemblies, door frames and paint and are responsible for transporting finished towers, so production schedules and throughput depend on the timeliness and quality of client-supplied inputs rather than the Company's own procurement.
- Borrowing levels requiring Rs. 11,500.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds for repayment/pre-payment — The principal object of the Fresh Issue is repayment and/or pre-payment, in full or part, of borrowings of Rs. 11,500.00 lakhs, indicating a leveraged balance sheet ahead of listing; RoCE (23.05% in FY26) sits well below RoNW (40.92%).
